newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY HOLDS JUST ABOVE RESISTANCE,WAITS FOR C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY HOLDS JUST ABOVE RESISTANCE,WAITS FOR C.BANK.

text.p: The zloty lingered just above the National Bank of Poland's recent intervention levels in morning Wednesday trade, but so far the central bank has refrained from forcing the local unit back below resistance.

Dealers said foreign capital inflows into Bank Handlowy's IPO, estimated at a minimum of $210 million, were placing the zloty under upward pressure, which will probably set off NBP interventions later on Wednesday.
"After early sales the market stabilised around 1.52 percent from parity with the NBP likely to intervene later in the session," said Piotr Czyzewski of ING Bank in Warsaw.
At 1000 GMT the zloty was at 1.56/1.51 percent from parity, flat from opening's 1.56/1.52 percent and slighly higher than Tuesday's close at 1.52/1.50 percent.
The zloty was at 3.2362/72 to the dollar, up from opening's 3.2365/80 and at 1.8756/67 to the mark, down from 1.8750/60.

Dealers said some foreign investors took advantage of the zloty's early highs around 1.55 percent from parity and sold $20 to $30 million of Polish T-bills in secondary trade, which pushed the zloty down from early highs.
"There was some light profit taking early in the day by foreigners," said one dealer at a large Polish bank.
Dealers said that foreign investors bid for minute amounts at Wednesday's 600 million zloty primary T-bill auction.

On the money market overnight and tomorrow next rates both eased 0.1 point from opening to 21.60/80 and 21.70/21.85 percent after the central bank refrained from staging any open market operations on Wednesday.
